2: 
3: Versions follow Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: ``MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH``, then an
4: optional pre-release (``-`` followed by dot-separated identifiers) and an
5: optional build (``+`` followed by dot-separated identifiers). Identifiers
6: are non-empty and made of ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens. Numeric parts
7: (MAJOR, MINOR, PATCH, and all-digit pre-release identifiers) must not have
8: leading zeros. Anything else is invalid and raises ``ValueError``.
9: 
10: Precedence (``compare``) follows the SemVer 2.0.0 rules: compare MAJOR,
11: MINOR, and PATCH numerically; a version with a pre-release is lower than
12: the same version without one; pre-release identifiers are compared left to
13: right, all-digit ones numerically and the rest in ASCII order, with
14: all-digit identifiers lower than the rest, and a shorter list lower when
15: all its identifiers equal the start of a longer one. Build metadata is
16: ignored.
17: 
18: Ranges (``satisfies``) are one or more comparator sets joined by ``||``; a
19: version satisfies the range if it satisfies any set. A set is one or more
20: comparators separated by whitespace, all of which must hold. A comparator
21: is a full version optionally prefixed by an operator:
22: 
23: - ``=`` (or no operator), ``>``, ``>=``, ``<``, ``<=``: by precedence.
24: - ``^X.Y.Z``: at least ``X.Y.Z`` and below the next version that changes
25:   the leftmost non-zero part, i.e. ``^1.2.3`` is ``>=1.2.3 <2.0.0``,
26:   ``^0.2.3`` is ``>=0.2.3 <0.3.0``, and ``^0.0.3`` is ``>=0.0.3 <0.0.4``.

28:

30: that set has a pre-release on the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (so
31: ``1.2.3-beta.2`` satisfies ``>=1.2.3-beta.1`` but not ``>=1.0.0``).

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from calendar import monthrange
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from decimal import Decimal


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Duration:
    years: int = 0
    months: int = 0
    weeks: int = 0
    days: int = 0
    hours: int = 0
    minutes: int = 0
    seconds: float = 0


_DURATION_RE = re.compile(
    r"P"
    r"(?:(?P<years>[0-9]+)Y)?"
    r"(?:(?P<months>[0-9]+)M)?"
    r"(?:(?P<weeks>[0-9]+)W)?"
    r"(?:(?P<days>[0-9]+)D)?"
    r"(?:T"
    r"(?:(?P<hours>[0-9]+)H)?"
    r"(?:(?P<minutes>[0-9]+)M)?"
    r"(?:(?P<seconds>[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)S)?"
    r")?"
)

_INTEGER_FIELDS = ("years", "months", "weeks", "days", "hours", "minutes")


def _invalid(text: str) -> ValueError:
    return ValueError(f"invalid ISO 8601 duration: {text!r}")


def _format_seconds(seconds: object) -> str:
    """Render seconds as a plain decimal, without floating point noise."""
    if isinstance(seconds, int):
        return str(seconds)

    value = float(seconds)
    if value.is_integer():
        return str(int(value))

    # repr() gives the shortest decimal that round-trips to the same float,
    # so values such as 1.5 print as "1.5" rather than a long binary artifact.
    text = repr(value)
    if "e" in text or "E" in text:
        # Expand scientific notation; ISO 8601 uses plain decimal notation.
        text = f"{Decimal(text):f}"
    return text


def parse(text: str) -> Duration:
    """Parse an ISO 8601 duration."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid ISO 8601 duration: {text!r}")

    match = _DURATION_RE.fullmatch(text)
    if match is None:
        raise _invalid(text)

    parts = match.groupdict()
    if all(value is None for value in parts.values()):
        raise _invalid(text)

    # A T must introduce at least one time part.  The regex above permits a
    # bare "PT", so check the groups explicitly.
    if "T" in text and all(
        parts[name] is None for name in ("hours", "minutes", "seconds")
    ):
        raise _invalid(text)

    seconds = 0.0
    if parts["seconds"] is not None:
        seconds = float(parts["seconds"])

    return Duration(
        years=int(parts["years"]) if parts["years"] is not None else 0,
        months=int(parts["months"]) if parts["months"] is not None else 0,
        weeks=int(parts["weeks"]) if parts["weeks"] is not None else 0,
        days=int(parts["days"]) if parts["days"] is not None else 0,
        hours=int(parts["hours"]) if parts["hours"] is not None else 0,
        minutes=int(parts["minutes"]) if parts["minutes"] is not None else 0,
        seconds=seconds,
    )


def format(duration: Duration) -> str:
    """Write ``duration`` in canonical ISO 8601 form."""
    for name in _INTEGER_FIELDS:
        value = getattr(duration, name)
        if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool) or value < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid duration part {name}: {value!r}")

    seconds = duration.seconds
    if isinstance(seconds, bool) or not isinstance(seconds, (int, float)):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid duration part seconds: {seconds!r}")
    if not math.isfinite(seconds) or seconds < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid duration part seconds: {seconds!r}")

    date_parts = []
    for name, suffix in (
        ("years", "Y"),
        ("months", "M"),
        ("weeks", "W"),
        ("days", "D"),
    ):
        value = getattr(duration, name)
        if value:
            date_parts.append(f"{value}{suffix}")

    time_parts = []
    for name, suffix in (("hours", "H"), ("minutes", "M")):
        value = getattr(duration, name)
        if value:
            time_parts.append(f"{value}{suffix}")
    if seconds:
        time_parts.append(f"{_format_seconds(seconds)}S")

    if not date_parts and not time_parts:
        return "PT0S"

    result = "P" + "".join(date_parts)
    if time_parts:
        result += "T" + "".join(time_parts)
    return result


def add(moment: datetime, duration: Duration) -> datetime:
    """``moment`` plus ``duration``."""
    total_months = (
        moment.year * 12
        + (moment.month - 1)
        + duration.years * 12
        + duration.months
    )
    year, month_index = divmod(total_months, 12)
    month = month_index + 1
    day = min(moment.day, monthrange(year, month)[1])

    moment = moment.replace(year=year, month=month, day=day)
    elapsed = timedelta(
        weeks=duration.weeks,
        days=duration.days,
        hours=duration.hours,
        minutes=duration.minutes,
        seconds=duration.seconds,
    )
    return moment + elapsed
